title: Adani Cement electrifies 410 trucks and puts diesel on the ropes

read.desc: Adani Cement prepares 410 electric trucks in India to reduce 11 million liters of diesel annually and more than 25,000 tons of CO₂.
paras: The first phase begins in Gujarat with electric trucks intended to move clinker and finished product. The schedule is demanding, and the announced figures are still a forecast, not savings already realized.

The deployment of Adani Cement started at the Sanghi facilities, in the state of Gujarat, in western India. The first industrial electric vehicles are used there to transport clinker—the intermediate material involved in cement manufacturing—and finished product.

The movement began on November 18 and represents the first incorporation of electric trucks into the company’s transport system. This is not a laboratory test with a shiny model: these are vehicles designed to enter the usual routes of an activity that moves heavy loads and depends heavily on diesel.

The first milestone is to have 410 electric trucks operational before the end of March 2027 . Until then, the 11 million liters of fuel that the company expects to avoid remain an estimate. The calculator is smiling, but the final bill has not yet arrived.

Adani Cement does not see Sanghi as an electric island. After this first phase, the company plans to extend the use of trucks to other plants and industrial routes across India, always within its materials transport logistics system.

title: ₹500 for 50 years of airport rights? Adani's Lucknow deal faces ₹249.63 crore stamp duty question

read.desc: Lucknow: How did a 50-year agreement granting a private company rights to operate, manage and develop a major international airport get executed on a stamp certificate worth just ₹500? And why did subsequent government assessments put the potential stamp duty...
paras: Lucknow: How did a 50-year agreement granting a private company rights to operate, manage and develop a major international airport get executed on a stamp certificate worth just ₹500? And why did subsequent government assessments put the potential stamp duty shortfall at ₹249.63 crore? These are among the questions arising from the concession agreement for Lucknow's Chaudhary Charan Singh International Airport, involving the Airports Authority of India (AAI) and Adani Lucknow International Airport Limited.

An investigation by New Delhi Post , based on official records obtained from the Uttar Pradesh Stamp Department, has uncovered a substantial discrepancy between the stamp duty paid when the agreement was executed and the liability subsequently assessed by government officials. The findings also bring the valuation of thousands of crores of rupees in airport land, the classification of the agreement and the treatment of public assets under scrutiny.

The concession agreement was signed on February 14, 2020, between the Airports Authority of India (AAI) and Adani Lucknow International Airport Limited. It covered 1,258.80 acres of airport land and granted the private concessionaire rights relating to the airport's operation, management and development for 50 years.

Yet, the original e-stamp certificate classified the document under Article 5 – General Agreement. The property description was recorded as 'Not Applicable', the consideration was shown as zero, and the stamp duty paid was just ₹500.

This raises a fundamental question: how was an agreement involving long-term commercial rights over a major public infrastructure asset treated as a general agreement rather than a document attracting stamp duty based on the nature and value of the rights being granted?

CEO Ashish Rajvanshi said that the system has been developed over 18 months, with the company building capabilities in engineering, integration, supply chains and lifecycle support.

The statement came after Bagheera AT1 successfully completed a No Cost No Commitment (NCNC) demonstration at the Pokhran Field Firing Ranges in Rajasthan on November 20. Senior representatives of the Indian Army, Department of Military Affairs and Ministry of Defence witness the demonstration, which validated day-and-night engagements, tandem missile firing and engagement of an aerial target at extended range.

The system is mounted on an Adani Defence-designed high-mobility armoured 4x4 vehicle, bringing together the missile, automated launcher and day-and-night sights into a complete mobile combat platform.

The company stated that the system can engage armoured targets at ranges of up to 8 km and uses laser beam-riding guidance, which is designed to offer high resistance to electronic jamming. Its tandem-firing capability allows two missiles to be launched in quick succession along the same beam, with the first intended to engage a tank’s active protection system and the second to strike its defences.

The platform carries four ready-to-fire missiles and eight reloads, giving it a total capacity of 12 missiles. Integrated thermal imaging and automated target tracking support day-and-night operations, while its shoot-and-move design is intended to reduce crew exposure after firing.

title: Anthropic’s $1.5 Tn Valuation Sparks Debate Between Uday Kotak And Adani CFO

paras: Adani Group Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Jugeshinder Robbie Singh has responded to banker Uday Kotak's comparison of artificial intelligence company Anthropic's USD 1.5 trillion valuation with the combined market capitalisation of India's top 10 companies, arguing that traditional businesses and AI companies cannot be valued using the same financial parameters.

In a post on X on 19 November, Singh described Kotak's comparison as a "textbook category error in asset pricing". He said conventional businesses are linked to human economic activity, while frontier AI companies represent a new economic model that can expand beyond the limitations of human labour and population growth.

Firstly, from @AdaniOnline congrats to @AnthropicAI Second, Cross-Regime Category Error: Why Legacy Bankers Can’t Price Synthetic GDP Comparing Anthropic’s $1.5T valuation to India’s top 10 corporates as "undervaluation"vs. "catching up" is a textbook category error in asset pricing. It benchmarks a convex call option on synthetic Labor in a new economic substrate against discounted cash flow (DCF) claims on a human-constrained economy. 1. The Ceiling of Human-Economy Equities Traditional blue chips (banking, energy, staples) are linear yield vehicles anchored to biological human GDP. Growth is capped by demographics, credit penetration, physical consumption, and waking hours—priced via mean-reverting multiples (P/E, EV/EBITDA). Calling them "undervalued" next to frontier AI is like calling Mumbai real-estate undervalued next to the discovery of thermodynamics. 2. Anthropic as a Call Option on Synthetic GDP (Yₛ) Cognitive labor is decoupling from human population growth. Frontier models aren't SaaS tools; they are the "infrastructure of intelligence" for a parallel synthetic workforce (Yₛ) operating above human output (Y_Total = Yₕ + Yₛ). At $1.5T, markets aren't capitalizing EBITDA. Using Black-Scholes intiution Wall Street is pricing implied volatility and right-tail convexity of a 24/7 digital workforce scaling at the marginal cost of compute. @AdaniOnline , we are already operationalizing this reality through our cobotic workforce model—a dual-track organizational architecture weaving human creativity with autonomous AI agents and robotics across our utilities, ports, and operations, upskilling 11000+ professionals annually to lead a ybrid industrial paradigm. 3. The 1999–2020 Precedent: Euphoria Still Underprices Regime Shifts In 1999, Mary Meeker and Dow 36,000 were mocked as peak-bubble delusion when global e-commerce was ~$150B, internet penetration was 5% (277M users), and $1T tech firms seemed impossible. When the NASDAQ peaked at 5,048 in March 2000 and crashed 78% (wiping out ~$5T and bankrupting https://t.co/cTFPLaPK4w and Webvan), legacy finance declared the thesis dead. Yet by 2020, reality crushed 1999’s wildest models: 4.5B+ internet users (57% of humanity), $4.2T+ in annual e-commerce, >60% digital ad share, and core winners (Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet) compounding into a $16T+ asset class. Legacy allocators mistook the 2000 clearing event for a ceiling, missing a new digital GDP layer. 4. The Epistemological Blind Spot of Legacy Bankers & Capital This is classic lender-mindset orthodoxy: mistaking backward-looking accounting ratios for capital creation. Allocators trained in capital-scarce banking worship trailing multiples, static book value, and incremental yield—dismissing any paradigm-building capex cycle that breaks 20th-century spreadsheet as a "bubble." While legacy finance debates scoreboards in the rear-view mirror, we have laid out our $100B+ (₹10 lakh crore) roadmap for the "Infrastructure of Intelligence"—mastering the full physical-to-digital stack from Port to Power to Metals to Processor, integrating gigawatt-scale renewable energy, grid transmission, and hyperscale liquid-cooled AI data centers (scaling toward 5 GW). Because intelligence is written in code, but it runs on electrons and sovereign infrastructure. India’s blue chips are neither undervalued nor "behind"—they are yield vehicles monetizing the physical human economy, while those building the energy-and-compute backbone are underwriting the new substrate of an add-on synthetic economy. You cannot measure a non-linear dimension with a static ruler built for the old world ( much like 2000, clearing out will occur here too). Scientifically, Ai is a bigger shift, akin to development of scientific method in 16th century thus an order of magnitude a greater opportunity.

title: Adani Cement to deploy 410 heavy-duty electric trucks

read.desc: Indian cement manufacturer Adani Cement (Adani Group) has announced plans to add 410 heavy-duty electric trucks to its fleet. It has already flagged off the
paras: Indian cement manufacturer Adani Cement (Adani Group) has announced plans to add 410 heavy-duty electric trucks to its fleet. It has already flagged off the first batch as part of the initiative and will commission the remaining trucks by March 2027.

Based on images shared with the announcement, Adani Cement appears to have procured eleven units initially. The company has deployed these heavy-duty electric trucks at its Sanghi plant in the western state of Gujarat and is using them to transport clinker and cement. It says the movement of both these materials is a carbon-intensive part of the cement industry’s operations.

The first batch comprises Chinese manufacturer Sany’s 55-tonne heavy-duty electric trucks. These units appear to be either the 5538E or the 5550E, the two 55-tonne high-roof models the company offers in India, both of which have a 4×2 drivetrain layout and pack 360 kW of power. The 5538E uses a 282 kWh battery pack that supports charging at up to 240 kW and delivers a range of 189 km. The 5550E upgrades to a 376 kWh battery pack that supports charging at up to 360 kW and increases the range to 245 km.

Adani Cement says the economics are now in favour of electric trucks in India’s cement industry. The company says that while diesel prices have increased by 60 per cent over the past decade, lithium-ion battery pack costs and solar tariffs have fallen by approximately 70 per cent and 47 per cent, respectively. It also states that diesel trucks emit approximately 737.5 grams of CO2 per kilometre. The company estimates its 410 electric trucks will reduce its diesel consumption by 11 million litres per year and avoid more than 25,000 tonnes of CO2 emissions annually.

Vinod Bahety, CEO of the Cement Business at Adani Group, said the company has identified multiple routes across the country for transporting clinker and cement using electric trucks. Its plan to deploy 410 electric trucks by March 2027 represents the first phase of electrifying these transport operations. By 2030, the company aims to expand its fleet to over 2,000 electric trucks and use them to handle 10 per cent of its road freight.

title: CERC Allows CSPDCL to Amend Adani Solar Safeguard Duty Claim

read.desc: CERC permits Chhattisgarh Discom to amend its ₹85.28 crore safeguard duty claim against Adani Solar under Change in Law provisions.
paras: The regulatory landscape governing India’s renewable energy sector often encounters disputes revolving around ‘Change in Law’ events. In a recent development, the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) has issued an order allowing the Chhattisgarh State Power Distribution Co. Ltd. (CSPDCL) to amend its petition involving a substantial ₹85.28 crore safeguard duty claim against Adani Solar Energy Jaisalmer One Pvt. Ltd. The core of the dispute traces back to the imposition and subsequent removal of safeguard duty (SGD) on imported solar cells, a fiscal element that directly impacts project economics and power purchase agreement (PPA) tariffs.

CSPDCL procures power from Adani Solar’s 450 MW solar project located in Rajasthan through an intermediary agreement with the Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI). The state distribution company contends that the expiration and removal of the 15% safeguard duty effective from 30 July 2021 constitutes a ‘Change in Law’ event under the PPA terms. According to CSPDCL, this regulatory shift reduced Adani Solar’s operational costs, and the resulting financial benefit should rightfully be passed on to the consumers in Chhattisgarh through a lower tariff or a direct refund of ₹85.28 crore along with applicable interest.

During the proceedings, CSPDCL sought to amend its petition to include a government notification dated 30 July 2018, correcting references that previously only highlighted a later notification from 29 July 2020. Adani Solar strongly opposed the amendment, arguing that the request was time-barred beyond the three-year limitation period, relied on assumptions rather than actual costs, and that the expiry of the 2018 notification was anticipated. However, CERC dismissed Adani’s objections as hyper-technical, classifying the amendment as a clarification rather than a novel case that prejudices the developer, while noting that Adani remains free to contest the substantive merits during the main hearings.

title: Adani Energy Solutions Secures Rs 500 Cr Bihar Transmission Project

read.desc: Adani Energy Solutions wins a Bihar transmission project linked to a 2,400 MW thermal plant, with annual tariff revenue of Rs 500 crore.
paras: Adani Energy Solutions has expanded its presence in India’s transmission sector after securing a Bihar project linked to the evacuation of power from a 2,400 MW thermal plant. The asset is expected to generate about Rs 500 crore in annual tariff revenue. The project falls under India’s tariff-based competitive bidding framework and will establish the transmission network for the Pirpainti Ultra Super Critical Thermal Power Plant in Bihar. The transmission system has a completion target of the fourth quarter of 2028.

The award adds another regulated transmission asset to Adani Energy Solutions’ portfolio as India steps up investment in power networks to accommodate new generation capacity and rising electricity consumption.

Asset Base Expands The Bihar project will add 881 circuit kilometres (ckm) of transmission lines and 3,160 megavolt-ampere (MVA) of transformation capacity to the company’s network. The company’s transmission portfolio will reach 30,683 ckm of lines and 146,585 MVA of transformation capacity after the addition. Its cumulative transmission capital expenditure will also rise to about Rs 91,500 crore. Vikramshila Power Transmission, a special purpose vehicle created for the transmission scheme, will implement the project.

Network Links Generation The transmission system will connect the Pirpainti generation complex with key nodes in Bihar’s power network. The scope covers new substations and high-voltage transmission corridors that will carry electricity from the upcoming thermal generation facility.

The scheme includes four gas-insulated substations (GIS) and transmission links at the 400 kV and 220 kV levels. The network will connect Pirpainti with Jhanjharpur and Begusarai, while additional links will strengthen connectivity with Bakhtiyarpur and other parts of the state’s transmission system.

Adani Energy Solutions Ltd (AESL) on Saturday announced that its wholly owned subsidiary, Powerpulse Trading Solutions Ltd (PTSL), had received a Letter of Award (LoA) from the West Bengal State Electricity Distribution Company Ltd (WBSEDCL) for supplying 1,750 MW of renewable power for 25 years. The agreement also includes a 750 MW greenshoe option, which, if exercised, would take the total contracted capacity to 2,500 MW.

Power supply for the initial 1,750 MW is scheduled to commence on July 1, 2028, while the additional 750 MW is expected from April 1, 2029, subject to the exercise of the option. According to AESL, PTSL emerged as the successful bidder following a competitive bidding process and an e-reverse auction. The company said it had tied up 4.6 GW of solar and wind capacity and 3.5 GWh of battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity to support its energy supply portfolio.

Reacting to the development, MAITC questioned the government’s priorities, alleging preferential access for corporate giants. The party said the state’s resources and long-term power contracts deserved transparency rather than preferential treatment.

Referring to national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee’s earlier criticism, MAITC asked who the government was accountable to, alleging that while some appeared to receive out-of-turn favours, ordinary people continued to struggle to access basic services.
